name: empty_chunk
why: A quiet tick reads zero bytes. Header only: 'no records' must not look like 'no output'.

name: basic_assistant
why: One assistant text record -> exactly one ASSISTANT_TEXT obligation over the whole line.

name: mixed_records
why: The five shapes a real transcript interleaves. Skips are recorded, not dropped.

name: crlf_frames
why: CRLF terminators and a bare CRLF blank line. Both terminator bytes stay inside [start,end).

name: blank_and_whitespace_lines
why: Empty is BLANK_LINE; whitespace-only is not empty, so it is MALFORMED_JSON, not BLANK_LINE.

name: partial_line
why: A chunk ending mid-record: PARTIAL_LINE, and next_offset stops at its first byte.

name: partial_line_multibyte
why: The chunk boundary lands inside a multi-byte sequence. Still one PARTIAL_LINE, no decode attempt.

name: multibyte_text
why: Ranges are byte offsets, so a multi-byte answer's end is past its character count.

name: malformed_and_nonobject
why: Non-JSON, truncated JSON, JSON that is not an object, and a line that is not UTF-8 at all.

name: timestamp_shapes
why: Both halves must agree on which of these parse. This is the corpus's most divergence-prone case.

name: empty_and_blank_text
why: A text block that trims to nothing is not an obligation; one non-blank block among many is.

name: schema_type_blocks
why: Off-schema `text`/`content` types. Rust reads them as absent; Python must not raise.

name: rotation_identity
why: Byte-identical to basic_assistant under a different incarnation: the output must differ.

name: base_offset_shift
why: Offsets are absolute file coordinates, not chunk-relative.

name: oversized_line
why: An unterminated run at or over the limit: OVERSIZED_LINE, and the cursor DOES advance.

name: oversized_after_complete
why: The limit is measured on the unterminated remainder alone, not on the whole chunk.
